result.title: Seeing Before Naming: Context-Grounded Learning of Novel Visual Concepts
result.summary: Learning an unfamiliar visual category requires more than adapting a classifier: the model must connect its visual evidence to a useful semantic name. A pre-trained vision-language model can retain discriminative image features while providing a weak textual anchor for the target concept. We address this imbalance through context-grounded semantic anchoring. Our framework, SynerNet, learns concept-specific name embeddings, exposes them to compatible linguistic contexts, and conditions their representations on visual evidence. Difficulty-aware processing and adaptive objective weighting coordinate this adaptation while retaining the pre-trained backbone. On four VISTA-Beyond domains, SynerNet reaches a mean 16-shot accuracy of 74.35%, compared with 72.45% for few-shot name learning. Across 14 domains in the name-masked transfer setting, it improves mean accuracy from 45.17% to 46.74%. Ablations identify concept-specific name embeddings and cross-modal context integration as important components. These results support treating concept acquisition as the construction of visually grounded semantic anchors.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SynerNet，在少样本条件下为新视觉类别学习概念专属的名称嵌入，用语言上下文与视觉证据对其表示进行条件化，并辅以难度感知处理和自适应目标加权，在 VISTA-Beyond 等设置上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 「以视觉证据条件化名称嵌入」与跨模态上下文融合可供核查 VLM 内部状态是否真正保留视觉细节、以及文本锚点与视觉信息之间的贡献分配；但该工作是分类适配而非推理期 latent 状态生成，与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 只有间接线索。
